subproblem.title: Total boundedness in U from the deformation theorem (Simon Ch. 6, 7.2, (1)–(3))
subproblem.statement: Assume the following five propositions. (DF) [the frozen statement of the sibling declaration cmc_deformation_theorem] For all P, m ∈ ℕ there is c ∈ [1, ∞) such that for every ρ > 0, compact K ⊆ ℝ^P and Λ ∈ [0, ∞) there is a finite set 𝒬̂ of currents in 𝒟_{m+1}(ℝ^P) such that every IM T ∈ 𝒟_{m+1}(ℝ^P) with spt T ⊆ K, M(T) ≤ Λ and M(∂T) < ∞ admits Q ∈ 𝒬̂, R ∈ 𝒟_{m+2}(ℝ^P) and S ∈ 𝒟_{m+1}(ℝ^P) with Q, ∂Q, R IM, T − Q − S = ∂R, Q = 0 or M(Q) ≥ ρ^{m+1}, M(Q) ≤ c·M(T), M(∂Q) ≤ c·M(∂T), M(R) ≤ c·ρ·M(T), M(S) ≤ c·ρ·M(∂T), spt Q ∪ spt R ⊆ thickening(3√P·ρ, spt T) and spt ∂Q ∪ spt S ⊆ thickening(3√P·ρ, spt ∂T) (masses and products in [0, ∞], M = M_{ℝ^P}). (BR) [the second conjunct of the frozen statement of cmc_closure_and_boundary_rectifiability] For all P, d ∈ ℕ, every open U ⊆ ℝ^P and every IM R ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(U) with M_V(∂R) < ∞ for every open V with closure(V) compact and contained in U, the boundary ∂R is IM. (IR) [conjunct (b) of the frozen statement of the sibling declaration cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub] For all P, n ∈ ℕ, every open U ⊆ ℝ^P, every IMRep R = (M, θ, ξ) in U and every Borel set E ⊆ ℝ^P, there are a current A ∈ 𝒟_n(U) and an IMRep R' in U with carrier M ∩ E, multiplicity θ and orientation ξ such that R' represents A. (IS) [conjunct (c) of the frozen statement of cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub] For all P, n ∈ ℕ, every open U ⊆ ℝ^P and IM A, B ∈ 𝒟_n(U), the current A − B is IM. (ME) [the frozen statement of the sibling declaration cmc_massOn_eq_imRep_measure] For all P, n ∈ ℕ, every open U ⊆ ℝ^P, T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) and IMRep R in U representing T: M_W(T) = R.measure(W) for every open W ⊆ ℝ^P. Let P, m ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open, K ⊆ U compact, Λ ∈ [0, ∞) and η ∈ (0, ∞]. Then there is a finite set 𝒬 ⊆ 𝒟_{m+1}(U) such that every integer multiplicity X ∈ 𝒟_{m+1}(U) with spt X ⊆ K, M(X) ≤ Λ and M(∂X) ≤ Λ admits Q ∈ 𝒬 and integer multiplicity R ∈ 𝒟_{m+2}(U), S ∈ 𝒟_{m+1}(U) with X − Q − S = ∂R and M(R) + M(S) ≤ η (M = M_U). Conventions: 𝒟_d(U) is the space of d-currents in U (SimonGMT GeometricCurrentOn U d) and 𝒟^d(U) the test d-forms in U (TestFormOn U d: smooth forms on ℝ^P with compact support contained in U); |α| is the Euclidean coefficient norm of a covector (covectorEuclideanNorm); M_G(X) = X.massOn G is the supremum of max(X(ω), 0) over ω ∈ 𝒟^d(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ G and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x (such ω are called admissible for M_G), and M(X) = X.mass = M_U(X) for X ∈ 𝒟_d(U); spt is the support of Simon 6.2.11 (GeometricCurrentOn.support); IM means integer multiplicity (contract IsIntegerMultiplicity), an IMRep R = (M, θ, ξ) is the contract structure IMRep with R.measure = θ·Hⁿ⌞M, R.action(ω) = ∫_M θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dHⁿ (⟨ω, ξ⟩ := ξ(x)(ω(x))) and R represents X when X(ω) = R.action(ω) for all test forms ω; subtraction of currents is the contract instance Sub; X ⇀ Y is WeaklyConvergesOn.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, proof of Theorem 7.2, the total boundedness (1) derived from the deformation theorem in (2), (3); step 4 of the parent proof, carried out for currents in U through the extension to ℝ^P and restriction back to U (step 3(c) and step 7 of the parent proof). Two elementary facts:
(F1) Mass subadditivity: for currents A, B with the same domain and every set G, M_G(A − B) ≤ M_G(A) + M_G(B). Indeed, if ω is admissible for M_G then so is −ω, (A − B)(ω) = A(ω) + B(−ω), and ENNReal.ofReal(s + t) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(s) + ENNReal.ofReal(t); take the supremum over ω.
(F2) Restriction to U. For Z ∈ 𝒟_d(ℝ^P) write Z|_U := Z.restrictDomain (subset_univ U); then Z|_U(ω) = Z(ω) for ω ∈ 𝒟^d(U) (regarded in 𝒟^d(ℝ^P)), (A − B)|_U = A|_U − B|_U, and M_U(Z|_U) ≤ M_{ℝ^P}(Z), since every form admissible for M_U(Z|_U) is admissible for M_{ℝ^P}(Z) with the same value. If Z is IM, so is Z|_U: let (M_Z, θ_Z, ξ_Z) be an IMRep of Z; (IR) in ℝ^P with E := U (open, hence Borel) gives an IMRep in ℝ^P with carrier M_Z ∩ U, multiplicity θ_Z and orientation ξ_Z. The same data form an IMRep in U (the carrier lies in U, local integrability over compact subsets of U is a special case of local integrability over all compact sets, and the remaining fields do not involve the domain), and it represents Z|_U: every ω ∈ 𝒟^d(U) vanishes outside U, so ∫_{M_Z∩U} θ_Z⟨ω, ξ_Z⟩ dH^d = ∫_{M_Z} θ_Z⟨ω, ξ_Z⟩ dH^d = Z(ω) = Z|_U(ω).
1. Let c ≥ 1 be the constant given by (DF) for (P, m). Choose ρ > 0 with 2c·ρ·Λ ≤ η: ρ := 1 if η = ∞, and ρ := η.toReal/(2c(Λ + 1)) otherwise (then 2cρΛ = η.toReal·Λ/(Λ + 1) ≤ η.toReal, so in [0, ∞] the inequality c·ENNReal.ofReal(ρ)·Λ + c·ENNReal.ofReal(ρ)·Λ ≤ η holds).
2. Apply (DF) to (ρ, K, Λ): there is a finite set 𝒬̂ ⊆ 𝒟_{m+1}(ℝ^P) with the deformation property. Let 𝒬 := {Q̂|_U : Q̂ ∈ 𝒬̂}, finite as the image of a finite set.
3. Let X ∈ 𝒟_{m+1}(U) be IM with spt X ⊆ K, M(X) ≤ Λ and M(∂X) ≤ Λ. The sibling extend_to_univ (applied with the assumed (IR) and (ME)) gives an IM Y ∈ 𝒟_{m+1}(ℝ^P) with Y|_U = X, spt Y ⊆ K, M(Y) ≤ M(X) ≤ Λ and M(∂Y) ≤ M(∂X) ≤ Λ < ∞. By (DF) there are Q̂ ∈ 𝒬̂, R̂ ∈ 𝒟_{m+2}(ℝ^P) and Ŝ ∈ 𝒟_{m+1}(ℝ^P) with Q̂ and R̂ IM, Y − Q̂ − Ŝ = ∂R̂, M(Q̂) ≤ c·M(Y) ≤ cΛ, M(R̂) ≤ cρ·M(Y) ≤ cρΛ and M(Ŝ) ≤ cρ·M(∂Y) ≤ cρΛ.
4. (Ŝ is IM.) By (F1), M(∂R̂) = M(Y − Q̂ − Ŝ) ≤ M(Y) + M(Q̂) + M(Ŝ) ≤ Λ + cΛ + cρΛ < ∞, so M_G(∂R̂) ≤ M(∂R̂) < ∞ for every open G (mass is monotone in the region). By (BR) applied with U := ℝ^P (open), d := m + 1 and the IM current R̂ ∈ 𝒟_{(m+1)+1}(ℝ^P), ∂R̂ is IM. Evaluating Y − Q̂ − Ŝ = ∂R̂ at any ω gives Ŝ(ω) = Y(ω) − Q̂(ω) − ∂R̂(ω), i.e. Ŝ = (Y − Q̂) − ∂R̂, which is IM by (IS) applied twice.
5. Put Q := Q̂|_U ∈ 𝒬, R := R̂|_U and S := Ŝ|_U; R and S are IM by (F2). For ω ∈ 𝒟^{m+1}(U), dω ∈ 𝒟^{m+2}(U) and (X − Q − S)(ω) = Y(ω) − Q̂(ω) − Ŝ(ω) = ∂R̂(ω) = R̂(dω) = R(dω) = ∂R(ω), using Y|_U = X. Hence X − Q − S = ∂R.
6. By (F2), M(R) + M(S) ≤ M(R̂) + M(Ŝ) ≤ 2cρΛ ≤ η. ∎
proof_key_steps: Fix ρ with 2cρΛ ≤ η and the finite family 𝒬̂ of (DF) for (ρ, K, Λ); 𝒬 is the set of its restrictions to U.
Extend X to Y on ℝ^P (sibling extend_to_univ) and deform: Y − Q̂ − Ŝ = ∂R̂ with M(R̂), M(Ŝ) ≤ cρΛ.
∂R̂ has finite mass, so it is IM by (BR), and Ŝ = (Y − Q̂) − ∂R̂ is IM by (IS).
Restricting Q̂, R̂, Ŝ to U preserves IM (via (IR)), the identity and the mass bounds.

Extension permits deformation against one finite family; finite boundary mass justifies BR before asserting that the remainder is IM. Domain restriction preserves the identity, IM property and mass estimates, giving precisely the stated conclusion.
